name: Jug of Hoegaarden ale
blurb: Courage at a groat a cup.

name: Flask of Malmsey
blurb: Sweet Cretan wine, the kind that ends in a wager.

name: Marchpane
blurb: Almonds and sugar pressed into the shape of a swan.

name: Box of sugared almonds
blurb: Bought for a lady; eaten on the way.

name: Linen bandages
blurb: Boiled, if you are lucky.

name: Venetian theriac
blurb: Sixty-four ingredients, viper flesh among them. Tobie disapproves and uses it anyway.

name: Qahwa of the Turk
blurb: A black bitter drink the Sufis take to stay awake. Unknown in Bruges; worth a great deal to whoever discovers it.

name: Cudgel
blurb: Ash, with a lump of lead knotted in.

name: Rondel dagger
blurb: Made for the gap between plates.

name: Falchion
blurb: A heavy single-edged blade, half sword and half cleaver.

name: Milanese arming sword
blurb: From the Missaglia workshops. The steel is the advertisement.

name: Steel arbalest
blurb: Spanned with a windlass. Astorre's men swear by them and at them.

name: Padded jack
blurb: Twenty layers of linen, stitched tight.

name: Cuir-bouilli cuirass
blurb: Boiled leather, hard as wood.

name: Brigandine
blurb: Small plates riveted inside velvet. A merchant's armour: it looks like a doublet.

name: Milanese harness
blurb: Full plate, fitted. You will be noticed.

name: Courier's satchel
blurb: The Charetty couriers' own pattern. Two more items home from abroad.

name: Pack mule
blurb: Stubborn, but she carries. Three more items home from abroad.

name: Bale of woad
blurb: Blue, from the Toulouse country.

name: Cask of Gascon wine
blurb: Bordeaux claret, which London drinks faster than it can pay for.

name: Sack of English wool
blurb: The Staple at Calais insists. Flemish looms insist louder.

name: Barrel of salt salmon
blurb: From Leith, where the Scots trade with anyone.

name: Bundle of stockfish
blurb: Dried cod from Iceland, hard enough to build with.

name: Bolt of Lucchese silk
blurb: Figured velvet the colour of blood.

name: Crate of Murano glass
blurb: Packed in straw and prayers.

name: Sack of alum
blurb: Every dyer in Flanders needs it. Every cardinal wants to own it.

name: Pot of kermes
blurb: Scarlet from insects. Worth more than its weight in most things.

name: Loaf of Cyprus sugar
blurb: From the Lusignan cane fields at Kouklia.

name: Chest of pepper
blurb: The trade everyone else's trade is measured against.

name: Pouch of gold dust
blurb: From beyond the desert, by the salt road.

name: Tusk of ivory
blurb: Carved into madonnas in Paris and sold back to Africa as relics.
